'''Dedric Nicholaus Lawson''' (born October 1, 1997) is an American-Lebanese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]] and the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].

==High school career==
Lawson attended [[Hamilton High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Hamilton High School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] alongside his older brother [[K. J. Lawson]]. As a freshman he averaged, 20.8 points, 13.4 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks per game. As a sophomore in 2013–14,  Lawson averaged 16.7 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.1 blocks per game. On September 11, 2014, Lawson [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] from the class of 2016 to the class of 2015 so he could join K.J. at [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/11508691/memphis-tigers-recruit-dedric-lawson-reclassifies-class-2015|title=Dedric Lawson joins class of 2015|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|date=September 11, 2014|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=October 22, 2023}}</ref> As a senior, Lawson averaged 21.9 points, 15.4 rebounds, 3.2 blocks and 2.1 assists per game. Dedric was soon selected to both [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Jason|title=Dedric Lawson named to McDonald's All-American Game roster|url=http://archive.commercialappeal.com/sports/tigers/basketball/dedric-lawson-named-to-mcdonalds-all-american-game-roster-ep-902345375-324473121.html|accessdate=April 28, 2018|work=[[Commercial Appeal]]|date=January 28, 2015}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Lawson was rated as a four-star recruit and considered one of the top prospects in the class of 2016, before reclassifying to the 2015 class.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/article/two-horse-race-for-2016-5-star-dedric-lawson-28404816/|title=Two horse race for 2016 5-star Dedric Lawson|last=Fisher|first=Chris|date=April 30, 2014|website=[[247Sports]]|access-date=October 22, 2023}}{{dead link|date=April 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Memphis, Dedric averaged 15.8 points and 9.3 rebounds per game and tied [[Keith Lee (basketball)|Keith Lee]]’s Memphis record for double-doubles by a freshman.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wade|first1=Don|title=What’s Expected of Dedric Lawson This Season? More Versatility, Fewer Hot nip Wings|url=https://www.memphisdailynews.com/news/2016/oct/28/whats-expected-of-dedric-lawson-this-season-more-versatility-fewer-hot-wings/|accessdate=April 28, 2018|work=[[Memphis Daily News]]|date=October 28, 2016}}</ref> Lawson was named [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|AAC Rookie of the Year]] as well as the Second Team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] as a freshman.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2016/3/7/MBB_0307164437.aspx |title= American Men's Basketball All-Conference And All-Rookie Teams Announced |publisher=American Athletic Conference |date=March 8, 2016 |accessdate=April 28, 2018}}</ref> As a sophomore, Lawson was named to the First Team All-AAC.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2017/3/6/MBB_0306175110.aspx|title=Men's Basketball All-Conference, All-Rookie Teams Announced|website=American Athletic Conference|access-date=April 28, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 19.2 points, 9.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game. In April 2017 he announced he was transferring to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] alongside K.J. and sat out a year as a redshirt per NCAA policy.<ref name="cbs"/> In late July he was suspended by Kansas coach [[Bill Self]] after being involved in an altercation and did not participate in the team's exhibition trip to Italy.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Newell|first1=Jesse|title=KU forward Dedric Lawson suspended for Italy trip following role in practice altercation|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article164484527.html|accessdate=April 28, 2018|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=July 30, 2017}}</ref>

During his lone season with Kansas, Lawson led the Big 12 in both scoring (19.4 ppg) and rebounding (10.3 rpg). Following Kansas' loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Lawson announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26470444/kansas-forward-lawson-entering-nba-draft|title=Kansas forward Lawson entering NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 8, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Austin Spurs (2019–2020)===
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Lawson was named in the [[Golden State Warriors]] roster for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/summer-league-2019|title=Warriors Announce 2019 NBA Summer League Roster and Broadcast Schedule|date=June 26, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=June 26, 2019}}</ref> He joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for training camp and ultimately was assigned to the Spurs’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AUSTIN SPURS ANNOUNCE 2019 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2019-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=December 5, 2019 |date=October 29, 2019 |archive-date=December 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211215225658/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2019-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 9, 2020, Lawson posted 33 points and 10 rebounds for his 10th double-double of the season during a 117–114 win against the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dedric Lawson, Chimezie Metu spark Austin Spurs over Oklahoma City Blue |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200309/dedric-lawson-chimezie-metu-spark-austin-spurs-over-oklahoma-city-blue |accessdate=May 22, 2020 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=March 9, 2020 |archive-date=April 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419230225/https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200309/dedric-lawson-chimezie-metu-spark-austin-spurs-over-oklahoma-city-blue |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished the season averaging 13.7 points and 8.1 rebounds in 42 games with Austin.

===Goyang Orion Orions (2020–2021)===
On July 9, 2020, the [[Goyang Orion Orions]] added Lawson to their roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=20-21시즌 외국인선수 영입 안내|url=https://orions.co.kr/orions/notice?uid=1115770&mod=document|date=July 9, 2020|work=orions.co.kr|accessdate=July 9, 2020|language=ko|archive-date=February 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224214021/https://orions.co.kr/orions/notice?uid=1115770&mod=document|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Beşiktaş (2021–2022)===
On June 2, 2021, he has signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/81211/dedric-lawson-besiktas-icrypexte.html|title=Dedric Lawson Beşiktaş Icrypex’te|last=|first=|date=June 19, 2021|website=bjk.com.tr|publisher=|language=Turkish|access-date=June 20, 2021}}</ref>

He played for the [[Atlanta Hawks|Boston Celtics]] in the [[2021 NBA summer league]], missing a single three point shot in his 4-minute debut, a 85–83 win against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in which he started.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|access-date=2021-08-08|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

==National team career==
In July 2025, Lawson was naturalized as a Lebanese citizen, and will join the [[Lebanon men's national basketball team]] for the [[2025 FIBA Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thisisbeirut.com.lb/articles/1320926/-basketball-who-is-dedric-lawson-the-new-lebanese|title=Basketball: Who is Dedric Lawson, the New Lebanese?|last=Haddad|first=Makram|date=July 18, 2025|website=thisisbeirut.com|access-date=August 10, 2025}}</ref>
